page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_2_v3 is an x86_64 server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon 8473C cores operating at 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The system is equipped with 1946.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 20.27 GB of RAM per core, and includes 4608 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. No graphics processing units are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities. The Passmark CPU score, extended instructions test, and encryption test all rank in the top 10 percent, alongside top-tier Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing results. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also reach the top 10 percent tier. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier read and write speeds for large blocks, although the Passmark memory score registers in the average tier. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the average category.

This server provides high memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets without the overhead of scaling out to multiple nodes. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though its Intel AMX support enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing. The hardware configuration is optimized for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive enterprise applications, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
